promise_band.headline: We Leave It Cleaner Than We Found It
promise_band.body: Ask anyone who has had a roof torn off: the mess is what they remember. Tear-off goes straight to the dumpster as we work, the whole yard and driveway get a magnet sweep for nails before we pack up, and we walk the property with you before we leave. seo_body.headline: Roofing In Dallas, Georgia
paragraphs: North Georgia is hard on roofs from both directions. Spring and summer bring the hail and straight-line wind that take shingles off outright, and the humidity does the slower damage — Gloeocapsa magma algae feeds on the limestone in asphalt shingles, which is what those black streaks on the north-facing slope actually are.

We handle both ends of that. Storm damage with the insurance claim managed from inspection through settlement, and soft wash roof cleaning that clears the algae without stripping the granules the way pressure washing does.
checklist: Residential and commercial roofing, repair through full replacement
Storm and hail damage with insurance claim handling
Soft wash roof cleaning, house washing and driveway cleaning
Solar installation planned around the roof's remaining life

faqs.q: Will my insurance actually cover a new roof?
faqs.a: It depends on your policy and on how the damage is documented. The most common reason a Georgia claim gets denied is the adjuster classifying storm damage as ordinary wear and tear, which happens most often when the damage is subtle or the roof already has some age on it. We photograph and measure everything before the adjuster arrives and meet them on the roof, so the claim is decided on a record rather than an impression.

faqs.q: A contractor offered to cover my deductible. Is that normal?
faqs.a: No — it is illegal in Georgia under HB 423, and it exposes you as well as the contractor. It is used as a closing tactic, so treat it as a warning about how that company operates. We quote the work honestly and you pay your deductible to your insurer as your policy requires.

faqs.q: Someone knocked on my door after the storm. Should I use them?
faqs.a: Be careful. Storm chasers follow weather into an area, work it hard for a season, and leave — and after one North Atlanta hailstorm the BBB logged around 30% more roofing complaints than normal. Legitimate local contractors rarely need to canvass door to door. Ask for a fixed local address, check how far back their reviews go, and get the estimate in writing before anyone signs anything.

faqs.q: What are the black streaks on my roof, and will pressure washing remove them?
faqs.a: Those streaks are Gloeocapsa magma, a blue-green algae that feeds on the limestone in asphalt shingles and causes granule loss over time. Do not let anyone pressure wash them off — the pressure strips granules and shortens the roof's life, and the algae grows back within weeks. A proper soft wash treats the algae itself and typically keeps the roof clean for three to six years.

faqs.q: Do I need a full replacement, or will a repair do?
faqs.a: Often a repair. A handful of wind-lifted shingles, a leak around a chimney or a failed pipe boot are all repairs, not replacements. We will tell you when that is the honest answer even though it is the smaller job — and we will tell you plainly when a roof is genuinely at the end of its life.

We are based in Dallas, GA and work across Paulding, Cobb, Douglas and Fulton counties — including Marietta, Kennesaw, Douglasville, Acworth, Smyrna and Roswell. If you are just outside that, call us and we will tell you honestly whether we are the right people for the job.

faqs.q: How much does the inspection cost?
faqs.a: Nothing, and there is no deposit to get a written estimate. We come out, get on the roof, and put a number in your hand. There is no same-day-only pricing and no pressure to sign while we are standing in your driveway.
